mainTopic: Blind judges and the הקש of ריבים to נגעים, then which foods are subject to טומאת אוכלין, מעשרות and פאה.
overview: The גמרא shows that the rule against a blind judge comes from רבי מאיר. In a ברייתא, he links ריבים (court cases) and נגעים (leprous marks) through one פסוק. Rules pass both ways: day only, no blind person, no relatives. A פסוק shows that one כהן is enough for נגעים, so the three-judge rule does not carry over. The גמרא then asks why רבי יוחנן did not object to a blind judge in his neighborhood. The answer is that he relied on another סתם משנה: money cases may be finished at night. That breaks the comparison to נגעים, and this משנה carries more weight. Two new משניות follow. Everything tithed can become טמא as food, but meat, fish and eggs become טמא without being tithed. Everything with פאה is tithed, but figs and vegetables are tithed without פאה, which the גמרא proves by comparing the conditions for פאה and for מעשרות. Garlic and onions do need פאה. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן begins a ruling about endives planted for animals and later meant for people, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר links disputes to leprous marks: both only by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names רבי מאיר as the source and quotes his ברייתא. A פסוק puts ריב and נגע together, so the rules of one carry over to the other. The first rule is that court cases, like נגעים, are handled only in the daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say, why does the פסוק say 'By their word shall every dispute and every leprous mark be'? What do disputes have to do with leprous marks? The פסוק compares them: just as leprous marks are looked at only by day, as it says 'on the day it appears,' so too court cases are judged only by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question of which תנא holds that a blind person cannot judge: it is רבי מאיר. It then starts quoting his ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר notices that one פסוק mentions court cases and נגעים together. He reads this as a הקש, a comparison that lets the rules of one apply to the other. The first rule moved over is the daytime rule, which goes from נגעים to court cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach? (or: the פסוק teaches)
Compares, linking two topics so the rules of one apply to the other (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
A dispute; here, a court case
A leprous mark that a כהן must look at

steps.whyThisMatters: This הקש is the source for the rules below about blind judges and relatives. The story about the blind judge at the end of this section depends on it.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir, as it is taught:
Rabbi Meir would say,
What does the verse come to teach

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כׇּל רִיב וְכׇל נָגַע״?
phrases.english: "According to their word shall every dispute and every leprous mark be"?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיָן רִיבִים אֵצֶל נְגָעִים?
phrases.english: What do disputes have to do with leprous marks?
It compares disputes to leprous marks:
just as leprous marks are viewed in the daytime,
as it is written: "And on the day it appears in him,"
so too, disputes are judged in the daytime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of who holds that a person blind in one eye cannot judge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a סומא באחת מעיניו may not judge?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר, based on his הקש of ריבים to נגעים.

steps.title: No blind person, for leprous marks or for court cases
steps.stepSummary: A blind כהן may not look at נגעים, because the פסוק speaks of the כהן's eyes. Through the הקש, a blind person may not judge court cases either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as leprous marks are not looked at by a blind person, as it says 'as far as the eyes of the כהן see,' so too court cases are not judged by a blind person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא carries a second rule from נגעים over to court cases: no blind person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'the eyes of the כהן' shows that the person doing the inspection must be able to see. Because of the הקש, the same requirement applies to a judge. This is the source the גמרא was looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind person
What the כהן's eyes see

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, a blind person may not judge. This comes from the הקש to נגעים.

phrases.english: And just as leprous marks are not viewed by a blind person,
as it is written: "As far as the eyes of the priest see,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:12. The word 'eyes' is plural, which hints that he needs sight in both eyes.

phrases.english: so too, disputes are not judged by a blind person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule drawn from the same הקש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blind person may not judge, just as a blind כהן may not inspect נגעים.

steps.title: The comparison works the other way too: no relatives
steps.stepSummary: Now the הקש runs from court cases to נגעים. A relative may not judge, so a כהן who is related to the person with the mark may not inspect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also compares leprous marks to disputes: just as disputes are not judged by relatives, so too leprous marks are not looked at by relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns the comparison around and moves a rule from court cases over to נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, rules went from נגעים to court cases. Here a rule from court law, that relatives may not judge, is applied to a כהן inspecting a נגע.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives, who may not serve as judges for their own family

phrases.english: And it compares leprous marks to disputes:
just as disputes are not judged by relatives,
so too, leprous marks are not viewed by relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the הקש in the opposite direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is a relative may not inspect the נגע of his relative.

steps.title: Should leprous marks also need three כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests carrying over another rule: court cases need three judges, so maybe נגעים need three כהנים. A קל וחומר seems to support this: if a money case needs three, a case about a person's own body should need three all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as court cases need three judges, should leprous marks also need three כהנים? It even makes sense: if a case about a person's money needs three, then a case about his body should need three all the more!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible problem with the comparison. Maybe it also means that נגעים need three כהנים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons are given for requiring three כהנים: the הקש itself, and a קל וחומר from money to the body. A נגע affects the person himself, which seems more serious than money. That makes three כהנים look logical.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then just as... (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
And it is logical (a reasoned argument)
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
His money / his body (his own person)

phrases.english: If so, just as disputes are judged by three,
so too, should leprous marks be viewed by three?
And it is logical:
if a case about his money needs three,
is it not all the more so for his body?
phrases.notes: A נגע affects the person himself, which seems more serious than a money case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the two-way הקש should go.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the הקש of נגעים to ריבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every court rule carries over, נגעים would need three כהנים, and a קל וחומר from money to the body backs this up.

steps.title: A פסוק shows one כהן is enough
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the person is brought to אהרן or to 'one of his sons.' This shows that a single כהן may inspect נגעים, so the three-judge rule does not carry over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall be brought to אהרן the כהן or to one of his sons, the כהנים.' So you learn that even one כהן may look at the נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the suggestion by quoting a פסוק that clearly allows one כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear פסוק overrides both the הקש and the קל וחומר on this point. The comparison still holds for daytime, blindness and relatives, but not for the number of people.

keyTerms.meaning: So you have learned
A single כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The הקש teaches day only, no blind person and no relatives. It does not teach three: one כהן is enough for נגעים.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And he shall be brought to Aaron the priest
or to one of his sons, the priests,"
so you have learned that even
one priest may view the leprous marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that three כהנים are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An explicit פסוק limits how far the הקש reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the הקש and the קל וחומר, נגעים would need three כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'one of his sons' show that one כהן is enough.

steps.title: A blind man judged near רבי יוחנן, who said nothing
steps.stepSummary: A story: a blind man lived in רבי יוחנן's neighborhood and judged cases. רבי יוחנן never told him anything about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain blind man in רבי יוחנן's neighborhood who used to judge cases, and רבי יוחנן did not say anything to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about a blind judge. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was silent, which seems to mean he allowed a blind person to judge. That looks like it clashes with what was just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind man (Aramaic)
His neighborhood
Was judging cases
Nothing at all

phrases.english: There was a certain blind man
who lived in the neighborhood of Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who would judge cases,
and he did not say anything to him at all.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, who never protested.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא סַמְיָא דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case about a blind judge, connected to the rule in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן let a blind man judge without protesting.

steps.title: How could רבי יוחנן allow it, given his own rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could stay quiet. He himself ruled that the הלכה follows an unnamed (סתם) משנה. The unnamed משנה being discussed here disqualifies a blind person from judging.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? Didn't רבי יוחנן say that the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's silence by pointing to his own general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that excludes a blind person from judging gives no name, so it is a סתם משנה. רבי יוחנן holds that a סתם משנה is the הלכה, so he should have stopped the blind judge. Step 9 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: How could he do this?
But didn't he say...? (introduces a contradiction)
The הלכה follows a משנה stated without a name

steps.confusionAlert: סתם משנה does not mean an unclear משנה. It means a משנה stated without naming who said it, which suggests it is the accepted view.

phrases.english: How could he do this?
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
The halakha follows an unattributed mishna!
phrases.notes: He means the unnamed משנה being discussed here, which does not let a blind person judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the behavior described in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's silence toward the blind judge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן follows a סתם משנה, and the unnamed משנה rules that a blind person may not judge, so he should have protested.

steps.title: The unnamed משנה that disqualifies a judge blind in one eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the unnamed משנה behind its question. רבי יוחנן himself explained that this משנה disqualifies a person who is blind in one eye from judging.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: anyone fit to judge is fit to testify, and there are people fit to testify but not fit to judge. We asked: who does this come to include? And רבי יוחנן said: it includes someone who is blind in one eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from the last step. It brings the exact משנה, and רבי יוחנן's own explanation of it, which shows that a blind person may not judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה. He also explained that this unnamed משנה rules out even someone blind in one eye from judging. So a fully blind judge should surely be ruled out, which makes his silence look even harder to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to serve as a judge
Fit to serve as a witness
What does this come to include?
Someone who is blind in one of his eyes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the proof for the question already asked in step 7: רבי יוחנן's own words seem to rule out a blind judge.

phrases.english: And we learned: anyone who is fit to judge
is fit to testify,
and there is one who is fit to testify
but is not fit to judge.
And we said: what does this come to include?
And רבי יוחנן said:
It comes to include one who is blind in one of his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text and רבי יוחנן's explanation that complete the question from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's silence about the blind judge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He rules like an unnamed משנה, and he explained this unnamed משנה as disqualifying even someone blind in one eye, so he should have objected to the blind judge.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן relied on a different unnamed משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן found another unnamed משנה: money cases are judged by day but may be finished at night. That משנה shows court cases are not fully like נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found another unnamed משנה, as we learned: money cases are judged during the day and may be finished at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן stayed quiet. He followed a different unnamed משנה that points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נגעים may only be looked at in daylight, but this משנה lets a money case be finished at night. That shows judging and inspecting נגעים are not fully alike. Since disqualifying a blind judge came from comparing the two, the source for disqualifying him falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed (סתם) משנה, stated without naming a sage
Money cases
The court may finish the case and give its ruling at night

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a comparison between two areas of law can be undone by one clear difference between them.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן found another unnamed משנה,
as we learned: money cases are judged by day,
and may be finished at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 7 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Competing source: a different unnamed משנה overrides the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן must follow the unnamed משנה that disqualifies a blind judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: He followed another unnamed משנה, which breaks the comparison between judging and נגעים, so a blind person may judge.

steps.title: Why does one unnamed משנה beat the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the משנה about money cases stronger than the משנה about who may judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes this unnamed משנה stronger than that unnamed משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the answer it just gave. Both sources are unnamed משניות, so why did רבי יוחנן pick one over the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule is that the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה. When two unnamed משניות clash, that rule alone cannot decide between them. The גמרא needs a reason to prefer one.

keyTerms.meaning: Its strength; what makes it stronger

phrases.english: And what is the strength
of this unnamed משנה over that unnamed משנה?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the משנה about money cases. 'That one' is the משנה about who may judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּהַאי סְתָמָא מֵהַאי סְתָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer of step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן prefers the משנה about money cases over the משנה about who may judge

steps.title: Two reasons the משנה about money cases wins
steps.stepSummary: First answer: an unnamed משנה that reflects many sages is stronger. Second answer: it appears in the section about the laws of courts, which is its home topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: an unnamed משנה of many sages is preferred. And if you want, say: it is because that משנה teaches this together with the laws of judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two separate reasons why רבי יוחנן relied on the משנה about money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: that משנה reflects the view of many sages, while the other follows a single sage. Reason two: that משנה appears among the laws of judges, which is its main subject, so it carries more weight on this question.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; used to offer a possible answer, often one of two
An unnamed משנה that reflects the view of many sages
Is preferred; carries more weight
The laws of judges and courts

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן did not object to the blind judge because he followed the unnamed משנה about money cases. It is stronger either because it reflects many sages or because it sits in its home topic, the laws of courts.

phrases.english: If you want, say: an unnamed משנה of many sages is preferred,
phrases.notes: The other משנה, about who may judge, was said earlier to follow only one sage, רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: and if you want, say:
it is because it teaches it
together with the laws of judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either (1) an unnamed משנה reflecting many sages is stronger, or (2) a ruling taught in its home topic, the laws of courts, carries more weight.

steps.title: New משנה: food that needs tithes can become impure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה states that any food that must be tithed can become טמא as food. Some foods can become טמא without needing tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything that must be tithed can become impure with food impurity. And there is food that can become impure with food impurity but does not need to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It follows the same pattern as the earlier one: 'all of group A belong to group B, but not all of group B belong to group A.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being obligated in מעשרות always means the item is a food that can receive טומאת אוכלין. The reverse is not true: some foods can become impure even though no tithes are taken from them. The group of impurity-capable foods is the wider one.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Tithes, portions of produce that must be set aside
The kind of ritual impurity that food can receive
Obligated

phrases.english: MISHNA
Anything that is obligated in tithes
can become impure with food impurity,
and there is something that becomes impure with food impurity
but is not obligated in tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of judges and witnesses ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything that must be tithed can receive טומאת אוכלין, but some foods that can receive טומאת אוכלין do not need tithes.

steps.title: What does the last clause of the previous משנה add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the last clause of the previous משנה comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which foods the משנה means when it says some foods can become טמא without needing tithes. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 12 said, "there are foods that become טמא but are not tithed." It did not name them. The גמרא wants to know which foods fit that description.

phrases.english: Gemara: To include what?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the last line of the משנה in step 12: some foods become טמא but are not tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the final clause of the משנה in step 12 includes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which foods can become טמא as food without being subject to מעשרות?

steps.title: Meat, fish and eggs
steps.stepSummary: The added foods are meat, fish and eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include meat, fish and eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the clause means meat, fish and eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat, fish and eggs are food, so they can become טמא as food. But they do not grow from the ground, so there is no tithe on them. That is why the טומאה category is wider than the מעשרות category.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat
Fish
Eggs

steps.whatToRemember: Every food that is tithed can become טמא. But some foods, like meat, fish and eggs, can become טמא and are never tithed.

phrases.english: To include meat, fish, and eggs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat, fish and eggs can become טמא as food but are not subject to מעשרות.

steps.title: Everything subject to פאה is also subject to tithes
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that whatever needs פאה also needs מעשרות, but some things need מעשרות without needing פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything that requires פאה requires tithes. And there are things that require tithes but do not require פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה compares two farming obligations, פאה and מעשרות. It says the מעשרות group is larger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the previous משנה, which compared טומאה with מעשרות. Here the smaller group is פאה: everything in it is also in the מעשרות group. But the משנה does not yet say which crops need מעשרות without פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: Mishnah: Anything that is obligated in פאה
is obligated in tithes,
and there is what is obligated in tithes
but is not obligated in פאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with the same structure as the one in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פאה applies only to things that also need מעשרות. Some crops need מעשרות but not פאה.

steps.title: What does the last clause add here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which crops need tithes but not פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as before, the גמרא asks what the last clause of the משנה refers to. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said some crops need tithes but not פאה, without naming them. The גמרא wants specific examples.

phrases.english: Gemara: To include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the final clause of the משנה in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which crops are subject to מעשרות but not to פאה?

steps.title: Figs and vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The added crops are figs and vegetables, which need tithes but not פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include figs and vegetables, which are not obligated in פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the clause means figs and vegetables. They are tithed, but they are not subject to פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא names the crops but has not yet explained why פאה does not apply to them. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fig (or fig tree)
Vegetables

phrases.english: To include a fig and vegetables,
which are not obligated in פאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Figs and vegetables need מעשרות but are not subject to פאה.

steps.title: The five-part rule for פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer by quoting a משנה that lists five conditions a crop must meet to be subject to פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: They stated a rule about פאה. Anything that is food, is guarded, grows from the ground, is harvested all at once, and is brought in for storage is obligated in פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת פאה as a source for its answer. That משנה gives five conditions a crop must meet before פאה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a crop fails even one of the five conditions, there is no פאה on it. Figs and vegetables each fail one condition, as the next step explains. That is why they can need tithes but not פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
Guarded, meaning someone owns it and watches over it
It grows from the ground
It is harvested all at once
It is brought in for long-term storage

phrases.english: As we learned: They stated a rule about פאה:
Anything that is food, and is guarded,
and grows from the ground, and is harvested all at once,
and one brings it in for storage, is obligated in פאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source showing why figs and vegetables are not subject to פאה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that figs and vegetables are not subject to פאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת פאה that lists the five conditions for פאה.

steps.title: What each condition leaves out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes through the five conditions one by one and names what each one excludes. This includes figs and vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Food" leaves out wild-grown woad and safflower. "Guarded" leaves out ownerless crops. "Grows from the ground" leaves out truffles and mushrooms. "Harvested all at once" leaves out the fig. "Brought in for storage" leaves out vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each of the five conditions by naming something it leaves out. The last two examples, figs and vegetables, finish the answer from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition removes a specific type of plant. Figs ripen at different times, so they are not harvested all at once. Vegetables do not keep, so they are not stored. Each fails one condition, so פאה does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out
Plants that grew on their own, without being planted
Woad and safflower, plants used for dye
Ownerless property
Truffles and mushrooms

steps.whatToRemember: פאה needs all five conditions: food, guarded, grows from the ground, harvested all at once, and stored. Figs fail "all at once" and vegetables fail "stored," so they are tithed but have no פאה.
steps.confusionAlert: Figs and vegetables still need מעשרות. They are left out only of פאה, not of tithes.

phrases.english: "Food" excludes wild-grown woad and safflower,
"and guarded" excludes ownerless crops,

phrases.aramaic: וְגִידּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ — לְמַעוֹטֵי כְּמֵהִים וּפִטְרִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: "and grows from the ground" excludes truffles and mushrooms,
"and harvested all at once" excludes the fig,
"and brought in for storage" excludes vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each condition in the משנה of step 18 and shows how figs and vegetables are left out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the five conditions leaves out a type of plant. Figs are left out because they are not harvested all at once, and vegetables because they are not stored.

steps.title: The tithe list leaves out two of the פאה conditions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about מעשרות lists only three conditions: food, guarded, and growing from the ground. It leaves out 'harvested all at once' and 'brought in for storage.' So figs and vegetables need tithes even though they don't need פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about tithes the משנה says: anything that is food, is guarded, and grows from the ground must be tithed. The conditions 'harvested all at once' and 'brought in for storage' are not mentioned there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof by setting the tithe list next to the פאה list from step 18. The tithe list is shorter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פאה list has five conditions and the tithe list has only three. The two missing conditions are exactly the ones that exempted figs (not harvested all at once) and vegetables (not stored). So these crops fail the פאה test but pass the tithe test, which proves the answer given in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe, the tenth part of produce that must be separated
It does not teach, meaning the משנה does not mention it

steps.whatToRemember: פאה needs five conditions and מעשרות needs only three. Figs and vegetables meet the three but not all five, so they need tithes but not פאה.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding tithe, we learned:
Anything that is food,
and is guarded, and grows from the ground
is obligated in tithes.
Whereas 'its harvest is all at once'
and 'one brings it in for storage' are not taught.
phrases.notes: These are the two conditions from the פאה list in step 18 that are missing here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by comparing the tithe conditions with the פאה conditions listed in steps 18 and 19.
steps.raayaObject: That figs and vegetables need מעשרות but not פאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מעשרות 1:1, which lists only three conditions for tithes

steps.title: Garlic and onions among the vegetables do need פאה
steps.stepSummary: Vegetables are usually exempt from פאה, but if they include garlic and onions, those are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were garlic and onions among them, they are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule that vegetables are exempt from פאה. Garlic and onions are an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most vegetables are exempt because they are not stored for a long time. Garlic and onions are stored, so they do meet all five פאה conditions. The exemption for vegetables is therefore not total.

keyTerms.meaning: Garlic
Onions
They are obligated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying onions are 'not vegetables.' They are still vegetables, but they are an exception to the vegetable exemption from פאה because they can be stored.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ בָּהֶם שׁוּמִים וּבְצָלִין — חַיָּיבִין,
phrases.english: If there were garlic and onions among them, they are obligated,
phrases.notes: 'Among them' means among the vegetables, and 'obligated' means obligated in פאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the vegetable exemption from פאה established in steps 17 to 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garlic and onions are obligated in פאה even though other vegetables are exempt.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about onion beds
steps.stepSummary: A משנה discusses beds of onions among vegetables. רבי יוסי says each bed needs its own פאה, and חכמים say one bed's פאה covers all. Both agree that onions need פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: beds of onions among the vegetables. רבי יוסי says: give פאה from each one. חכמים say: give from one for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that onions need פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי and חכמים only argue about how to give פאה: separately from each bed, or once for all. Neither side doubts that onions need פאה at all. That shared assumption is the proof for step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Garden beds
From one for all, meaning one portion covers every bed
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: As we learned: beds of onions that are among the vegetables,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: פֵּאָה מִכׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: פאה from each and every one;
and the Rabbis say: from one for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 21 that onions are obligated in פאה.
steps.raayaObject: That garlic and onions are obligated in פאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פאה 3:4 about onion beds, where both sides assume פאה applies

steps.title: Endives first planted for animals, then meant for people
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן about endives planted for animal feed when the owner later decided to use them for people. The ruling itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: endives that someone first planted for animals, and then changed his mind and decided they are for people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new statement and setting up the case. The ruling is not given yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something grown for animals is not human food at first. Here the owner's plan changes partway, from animal feed to human food. רבי יוחנן's ruling, which comes next, will tell us how that change affects the endives' status as food.

keyTerms.meaning: Endives, a leafy vegetable
Animal, here meaning animal feed
He changed his mind

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
endives that one planted at first for an animal,
and then reconsidered them for people

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement about whether a plant counts as food when the owner's intended use changes, after the discussion of פאה exemptions ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up (endives planted for animals, then meant for people). The ruling follows in the continuing text.
